analyst_view.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, one win in their last six in all competitions) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban after his appeal failed (counted), Fabio Carvalho may return from a knock (the numbers still count him as out), and captain Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring, not in the numbers' list) are out for weeks after injuries on international duty, with Henry, Furo, Dasilva and Milambo also missing. Keith Andrews calls Callum Wilson the obvious replacement up front, with Schade another option, and Diouf or Lewis-Potter at left-back. David Moyes has a fully fit squad, Jack Grealish back after his disciplinary absence and likely on the bench, and Thierno Barry (10 goals in 13) up front. Brentford have conceded only three league goals at home, Everton have won one of five away, and referee Craig Pawson (3.7 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban and about 4% for Carvalho, who may in fact be back from his knock. They also can't see that Brentford lose two first-choice defenders, Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry and an Everton side with Grealish available again. Brentford's strong home defence (three conceded) and Everton's poor away form keep this mild: about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. The reshuffled Brentford left side (Diouf or Lewis-Potter at left-back for Hickey) changes who supplies the width rather than how much, and Everton's expected 4-2-3-1 is their usual shape, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered for referee Craig Pawson (3.7 a game in his record) and calm past meetings. No Everton player is reported suspended, Everton have no injuries, and there is no needle between the sides beyond a tight table, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson, who scored in all three Carabao Cup games, starts up front and Carvalho may return, while a weakened Brentford back line should let Everton shoot a little more, so the two balance and I stay at 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Wilson leading the line and Everton's Barry facing a reshuffled back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.
